content: Glyburide is a medication prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not produce enough insulin or cannot effectively use it, leading to uncontrolled blood sugar levels. It is particularly used in individuals whose diabetes cannot be managed by diet alone. Glyburide works by stimulating the pancreas to release insulin and improving the body's ability to use insulin efficiently. However, for this medication to be effective, the pancreas must still be capable of producing insulin. Glyburide is not suitable for treating type 1 diabetes, a condition where the body does not produce insulin at all. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Glyburide is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken once daily with breakfast or twice daily if a higher dose is required. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take glyburide exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before starting glyburide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to glyburide or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), dexamethasone, diuretics, estrogens, isoniazid, MAO inhibitors, medications for high blood pressure or heart disease, metformin, niacin, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, prednisone, probenecid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking glyburide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking glyburide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate drowsiness caused by glyburide, so use it cautiously. Inform your doctor if you use tobacco products, as smoking may reduce the effectiveness of glyburide. Additionally, avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as glyburide may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet, and consult your doctor about the safe use of alcohol, as it may lower blood sugar levels. If you forget a dose of glyburide, ask your doctor in advance what to do. As a general rule, take the missed dose as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Glyburide may cause changes in blood sugar levels. Be familiar with the symptoms of low (hypoglycemia) and high (hyperglycemia) blood sugar and know how to respond. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, nervousness, irritability, sudden mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. If untreated, severe symptoms such as confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness may occur. Your doctor will provide instructions on how to manage hypoglycemia, such as checking your blood sugar, consuming sugary foods or drinks (e.g., hard candy or fruit juice), or seeking medical care. Ensure that family, friends, and others around you are aware of these symptoms and know how to get medical help if needed. Symptoms of hyperglycemia include extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. If untreated, hyperglycemia can lead to a serious, life-threatening condition called diabetic ketoacidosis. Symptoms of ketoacidosis include dry mouth, upset stomach, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Glyburide may also cause severe side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience a skin rash, itching, redness, exaggerated sunburn, yellowing of the skin or eyes, light-colored stools, dark urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, fever, or sore throat. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store glyburide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Studies have shown that individuals taking oral antidiabetic drugs may have a higher risk of death from heart problems compared to those managing diabetes with diet and insulin. Discuss the potential risks, benefits, and alternatives of glyburide with your doctor. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring of blood sugar and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels. Your doctor will also instruct you on how to monitor your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Always wear a diabetic identification bracelet to ensure proper treatment in emergencies. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
